messages.subject: Re: Scaled chi-square difference tests - the 3 options lead to different conclusions
parts:
The satorra.bentler.2010 statistic is clearly wrong. But I think this
approach cannot handle 'nested' models that are only nested in the
covariance sense, but not in the parameter-table sense. If you compare a
unidimensional/1-factor model to a two-factor model, then the parameter
tables look very different. The satorra.bentler.2010 approach, however,
requires that the parameter tables are compatible. The idea is that we
plug in the values of the restricted model in the less-restricted model.

Could you show us the lavaan syntax for the three models?

Yves.

messages.author: 38b9f0217d9f5653
messages.subject: Re: Scaled chi-square difference tests - the 3 options lead to different conclusions
parts:
The code I used is below and the data is attached should that be helpful.
The variables a to z are the letters of the alphabet and the scores are how well kindergarten children could form the letters when tested at various times in their learning cycle (times 1 to 3).

library(lavaan)
library(semTools)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
       
data1=read_excel("LFA confirmatory factor analysis.xlsx",sheet="Data for R" )
head(data1)

# Make a version of the data with letter variables defined as ordinal
data2=data1
data2[,5:30] <-  lapply(data2[,5:30], ordered)

# Single factor
dim1 <- 'f1 =~ a + b + c + d + e + f + g + h + i + j + k + l + m + n + o
+ p + q + r + s + t + u + v + w + x + y + z
'

# Two factors based on the results of the EFA
dim2 <- '
f1 =~e + x + a + g + c + q + y + w + d + u + s + v + z + h + b + j + o
f2 =~ f + i + p + t + r + n + l + m + k
'

bifactor <- '
# General factor
general =~ a + b + c + d + e + f + g + h + i + j + k + l + m + n + o
+ p + q + r + s + t + u + v + w + x + y + z

# Individual uncorrelated factors (as per the correlated factors model)
f1 =~e + x + a + g + c + q + y + w + d + u + s + v + z + h + b + j + o
f2 =~ f + i + p + t + r + n + l + m + k

general ~~ 0*f1
general ~~ 0*f2
f1 ~~ 0*f2
'
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Final models and reliability analyses used for the paper - using polychoric correlations

# Single dimension
f1.ord <- cfa(dim1, data = data2)
summary(f1.ord, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

# Correlated factors model - equivalent to EFA model
f2.ord <- cfa(dim2, data = data2)
summary(f2.ord, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

# Bifactor model
f3.ord <- cfa(bifactor, data = data2)
summary(f3.ord, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

## Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.2000") when no option is specified
co123=compareFit(Bifactor = f3.ord, Correlated = f2.ord, Unidimensional = f1.ord,moreIndices = T,nested=T)
summary(co123)

## Request the simple approximation of Sattora & Bentler 2001
co123a1 <- compareFit(Bifactor = f3.ord, Correlated = f2.ord, Unidimensional = f1.ord, moreIndices = T,
                      argsLRT = list(asymptotic = TRUE, method = "satorra.bentler.2001"),nested=T)
summary(co123a1)

## Request the strictly-positive robust test statistics of Sattora & Bentler 2010 - made no difference choosing asymptotic=F
co123a <- compareFit(Bifactor = f3.ord, Correlated = f2.ord, Unidimensional = f1.ord, moreIndices = T,
                   argsLRT = list(asymptotic = TRUE, method = "satorra.bentler.2010"),nested=T)
summary(co123a)

Thanks,
Kim
